source.title: BROW: Better featuRes fOr Whole slide image based on self-distillation
source.authors: Yuan Wu; Shaojie Li; Zhiqiang Du; Wentao Zhu

record.tranche_reason: Tests model-scale effects on downstream image-model tasks, extending the scale-to-downstream-performance question to whole-slide-image models; it does not measure language-model pretraining loss.
record.gate_note: The study reports comparisons between model scales on downstream WSI tasks, recorded under V6. General statements and citations about scaling in other work are not rows. It does not report held-out pretraining cross-entropy, power-law fits, extrapolation from smaller runs, or a compute-optimal allocation.
record.test_reason: This is a method paper for a pathology foundation model (BROW). It cites Kaplan et al. as motivation and reports a few two-point size comparisons on downstream vision tasks. It reports no pretraining loss, no scaling fit and no predictability analysis. The Res50 vs ViT-b comparison changes architecture family (CNN to transformer) along with size, and no parameter counts are given. Only BROW ViT-s vs ViT-b is a pure size comparison, and it is a single pair in a non-language vision system. None of these results measure what any version names, so they go under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right, but the main conclusion is that BROW is an effective, robust WSI foundation model, credited to a large dataset, scaled-up model size and the training framework. The authors also attribute the drops for Res50 pretrained on WSIs on BRCA/RCC to limited model capacity, and ViT-b's fine-tuning shortfall to overfitting on limited data, which efficient fine-tuning mitigated.
record.recipe_differences: The study compares visual-model sizes using downstream classification and segmentation metrics, rather than fitting held-out language-model cross-entropy scaling laws or testing compute-optimal allocations.
record.method_sensitivity: The BROW scale comparison changes direction between linear evaluation and full fine-tuning on CoNSeP; the authors suggest limited fine-tuning data and overfitting may explain the reversal.

fits_no_version.finding: Moving from ResNet50 to ViT-b as a DINO-pretrained feature extractor raises slide-subtyping ACC/AUC on all 5 datasets and both aggregators, by up to +7.5% ACC.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In pathology MIL, larger transformer feature extractors outperform smaller CNN extractors on downstream tasks (architecture and size confounded).

fits_no_version.finding: BROW ViT-b beats ViT-s slightly under linear probing but falls slightly below it under full fine-tuning on small CoNSeP data. Parameter-efficient fine-tuning or added data recovers ViT-b's performance.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The downstream benefit of a larger vision backbone depends on the adaptation method and the amount of fine-tuning data.

record.problems: The results are downstream metrics rather than held-out pretraining loss; parameter counts and compute budgets are not stated. No uncertainty estimates are reported. Scale comparisons are limited to the tested architectures, datasets, and training stages.

untested.parts: No pretraining loss vs parameters, tokens or compute.
No shape comparison at fixed parameter count.
No power-law fit in the vision setting.
No predictability of downstream performance from scale or loss; only two-point comparisons, with architecture confounded in the Res50 vs ViT-b comparison.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'tests/T3 with V6 supports/challenges' is downgraded. These are sparse two-point downstream comparisons in a pathology vision model, with no parameter counts and no loss, and the main comparison is confounded by architecture. No verdict labels are given. The values in the rows match Tables III and VIII. Rows are grouped by range in row_fixes.

versions.untested_parts: No held-out pretraining loss sweep over parameters, tokens, or compute.
No loss extrapolation from small runs to larger runs.
No fixed-compute allocation comparison or parameter/token growth trends.
No comparison of architectures at fixed parameter count measuring pretraining loss.
The study uses image models but does not test whether a power-law loss form holds in another modality or regime.
Tests downstream task metrics across model scales in selected WSI settings, not prediction from pretraining loss or a general quantitative scaling law.
No comparison of loss-fitting choices, exponents, or fit-dependent compute-optimal splits.
